article:
Hands, not vibes

A model without tools can only talk. MCP — Model Context Protocol — is a way to give it hands: read this repo, send this mail, check this calendar. An agent is that loop left running: look, act, look again, sometimes while you are asleep.

You already felt a primitive version. The edit button on this page is a hand. A Grok bot with a schedule is a hand. Do not start by building a swarm. Start by giving one model one tool you would trust overnight.

What is worth automating

Things that already have a rule. “If the preview is red, paste the log.” “If a mark lands, I do not need a Slack.” “If a shop is quiet, draft the order — do not send it.” The last five words matter. Agents should draft. People should fire.

How I actually do it

Meeting Mode is the honest test: a ritual, a dated note, optional listening. If an agent joins the call, it is a guest with a notebook, not a boss. The bots idea on X is the same pattern — standing duties, not a second personality.

I would rather one reliable hand than eight clever ones that fight.

Where noobs get stuck

Agents that can spend money. Agents that email your whole list. Agents with no log. Or a weekend spent on “multi-agent architecture” before a single tool works twice.

Film this

Give Grok one tool on camera — list the files in a folder, or post a draft, not a live blast. Watch it use the hand. Then unplug the hand and show the model reduced to talk again.

Do this before chapter 16

  • Name one job you would let run while you make tea.
  • Give the model the smallest tool that job needs.
  • Log every action. Read the log once.
  • Do not let it send, charge, or delete without you.

Next: design and video — look, clips, Imagine. Distribution is part of shipping.
